subject.title: fix(agents): preserve safe JavaScript and TypeScript in Code Mode

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this parser-backed module-access validator and production Acorn dependency as the Code Mode sandbox boundary after direct Codex-runtime and packaged-install confirmation?
rationale: This is not only a regression fix: it changes the policy gate that protects the isolated guest from executable module access, so maintainers must confirm the permanent boundary and dependency ownership.

options.title: Request boundary proof before merge
options.body: Require direct confirmation against the actual Code Mode wrapper, upstream Codex runtime contract, packaged dependency resolution, and redacted real-worker output for safe and blocked cases.

options.title: Accept the reviewed boundary
options.body: Approve the parser-backed approach if maintainers independently verify its parser modes and failure behavior match the intended sandbox contract.

options.title: Pause for a narrower design
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers prefer a shared AST-policy helper or another owner boundary before making Acorn a production dependency.

recommendation.title: Request boundary proof before merge
recommendation.body: Require direct confirmation against the actual Code Mode wrapper, upstream Codex runtime contract, packaged dependency resolution, and redacted real-worker output for safe and blocked cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied PR and security-review context connect steipete to the proposed Code Mode boundary and dependency promotion.
